articles.title: 菲尔兹奖得主博尔彻兹取消计分家庭作业：AI 作弊泛滥，仅线下考试可行
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，加州大学伯克利分校（UC Berkeley）一名教授宣布，不再给学生布置计分家庭作业，原因是人工智能（AI）的滥用让这类作业失去了意义。据《纽约邮报》（New York Post）10 月 26 日报道，知名数学家、菲尔兹奖得主理查德 · 博尔彻兹（Richard Borcherds）表示，如今几乎无法分辨学生提交的作业究竟是自己完成的，还是借助人工智能生成的。因此，他现在主要通过不允许使用电子设备的线下考试来评估学生的学习情况。IT之家注意到，博尔彻兹在接受该媒体采访时表示：“如今，在线考试已经是在浪费时间，因为有些学生会直接使用 AI 回答问题。我无法判断哪些学生使用了 AI，但我注意到，在线考试的平均分数大幅提高。”他还指出：“按照答案是否正确来评分，会给学生使用 AI 完成家庭作业、而不是亲自解题提供巨大的动力，同时还会惩罚那些诚实完成作业的学生。花费时间和金钱为 AI 生成的答案评分，也是一种浪费。”对于这一问题，加州大学伯克利分校此前已经考虑过使用 AI 检测软件，但最终认为这类工具的可靠性不足。因此，校方决定将 AI 使用政策的制定权交给教授，只要求他们在课程大纲中明确说明相关规定。至于博尔彻兹，他表示，如果 AI 最糟糕的影响只是增加教师批改学生作业的难度，那他就“非常放心了”。

articles.title: 火狐 Firefox 浏览器 159 稳定版发布：修复 167 个漏洞，侧边栏增“已保存密码”默认按钮
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，Mozilla 昨日（10 月 27 日）发布公告，宣布推送火狐 Firefox 浏览器 159.0 稳定版，覆盖 Windows、macOS、Linux 和移动端；官方同时更新了长期支持版本 Firefox 153.6.0 和 115.44.0。安全更新方面，Firefox 浏览器 159 共计修复 167 个安全漏洞，其中包括 108 个高危漏洞。多数问题与内存处理相关，例如缓冲区溢出、释放后使用等缺陷。Mozilla 敦促仍在使用旧版本 Firefox 的用户应尽快升级。功能方面，Firefox 159 在侧边栏新增了“已保存密码”默认按钮，用户可以更快访问浏览器中保存的登录信息。IT之家附上相关图片如下：在苹果 macOS 平台上，新版 Firefox 浏览器调用 macOS 原生的分享选择器，会在隔空投送、信息和其他应用旁边显示页面预览和最近联系人，还可以同时分享多个选定的标签页。在 Smart Window 聊天中输入 /watch，可让 Firefox 监控价格下降、补货等页面变化，并在发现变化时发送桌面通知；监控任务可在工具栏 Tasks 或 about:smartwindowtasks 管理。该功能仍属 Beta，据报道目前限美国、加拿大和法国。快捷按键方面，Windows / Linux 使用 Ctrl+Shift+A 搜索已打开标签页，macOS 为 Cmd+Shift+A；扩展与主题快捷键改为 Ctrl+Shift+F / Cmd+Shift+E。开发者方面，Firefox 159 支持滚动驱动动画，并新增 animation-timeline、scroll-timeline、view-timeline 和 animation-range 等 CSS 属性，可用于制作随页面滚动触发的进度条或动效。浏览器还支持独立的自定义元素注册表，避免不同前端库在同一页面使用相同元素名时发生冲突。参考火狐 Firefox 浏览器 159 稳定版更新日志点此访问 Mozilla 官方服务器下载 Firefox 浏览器 159 稳定版

articles.title: 马斯克坚定看好内存需求，称机器人所需内存将超过其他任何领域
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，特斯拉 CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克于 10 月 27 日在社交平台 X 上表示，机器人对内存的需求将超过地球上其他所有一切，驳斥了市场关于人形机器人对内存需求不大的观点。Counterpoint 分析报告称，到 2030 年，人形机器人 DRAM 需求将增长 20 倍，达到 172,000 TB，每台机器人的内存容量翻倍至 39 GB。Futurum Equities 分析师 Shay Boloor 估计，如果特斯拉每年生产 1000 万台 Optimus 人形机器人，每台搭载 72 GB 内存，年内存需求约为 720 PB，他认为机器人采用 LPDDR 而非 HBM 将为美光和 SK 海力士创造更大的出货机会。马斯克还表示，超级智能的计算需求将远远超过机器人本身，但几乎 100% 的超级智能计算最终将在深空完成。IT之家注意到，美光 CEO Sanjay Mehrotra 上个月也表示，到 2030 年左右，物理 AI 可能成为内存和存储需求的重要驱动力。关于生产时间表，马斯克在公司最近第三季度财报电话会议上表示，Optimus 机器人的首批客户交付目标定在明年年底左右，而弗里蒙特生产线至少还需要一年时间才能达到每周 2 万台产能。

articles.title: 消息称 Solidigm 计划在美斥资 450 亿美元建设 NAND 晶圆厂
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，彭博社当地时间昨日报道称，SK 海力士完全控股的 NAND 与 SSD 企业 Solidigm（思得）正就在美新建晶圆厂事宜与美国商务部洽谈。Solidigm 计划为此投资 450 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,006.47 亿元人民币），并最终有望扩展近 1000 亿美元。消息人士透露，潜在的建厂地址包括纽约州在内的多个州，晶圆厂最早可能明年动工。该企业目前采用“双头”业务结构：在美设有总部和研发设施，中国则是其唯一量产晶圆厂所在地。Solidigm 计划先在中国实践新技术然后转移至拟设的美国晶圆厂，但这需要得到美国商务部的许可。

articles.title: 微软 Surface Duo 2 变“苹果 iPhone Duo”：铺路原生运行 iOS 26，双屏触控已可用
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 昨日（10 月 27 日）发布博文，分享了来自开发者 @none24smu 的更多图片，展示了微软 Surface Duo 2 手机成功运行 iOS 26 系统。iOS 26 已在微软 Surface Duo 2 上原生运行。微软 Surface Duo 2 是微软于 2021 年推出的双屏安卓手机，也是 Surface Duo 系列的第二代、也是最后一款产品。它采用两块 5.8 英寸 OLED 屏幕通过铰链相连，展开后形成约 8.3 英寸的“双屏平板”体验。需要注意的是，本次并非通过模拟器实现，开发者在 Surface Duo 上原生运行苹果 iOS 26 系统，而且在今天（10 月 28 日）发布的推文中，还表示正适配 iOS 27 系统。在实现方式上，开发者利用苹果开源的 XNU 内核和自定义 UEFI 加载器完成移植，并将该设备识别为“iPhone 17 Pro Max”。开发者需要从源代码编译 XNU 内核，为高通处理器编写驱动，并构建 Metal 图形 API 到 Vulkan 的转换层，让 Surface Duo 2 的 Adreno 660 GPU 能运行 iOS 图形指令。Surface Duo 2 两块屏幕上的 iOS 26 语言选择器，并叠加显示启动日志。iOS 在安卓手机上启动。由于骁龙 888 不支持苹果的指针认证机制，开发者还移除了约 2,960 万个指针签名，并将部分 arm64e 代码改写为 arm64。IT之家附上相关图片如下：开发者写道：“两个显示器都以 37fps 的帧率运行 —— 以前是 3-10fps”，紧接着又写道：“触摸功能正常了！”，这简直太棒了。在该开发者分享的图片中，Surface Duo 移植 iOS 26 系统后，在设置应用中的“关于本机”页面显示系统版本为 iOS 26.5.2，型号为“iPhone 17 Pro Max”，内存容量为 5GB，序列号、Wi-Fi 地址和蓝牙信息均显示为“N/A”。Surface Duo 2 上的 iOS 26.5.2 在“设置”中显示为 iPhone 17 Pro Max。据报道，移植版 iOS 26.5.2 已能同时点亮 Surface Duo 2 的两块屏幕，触控功能也可正常使用。系统将双屏视为一个整体画布，“设置”等应用可跨屏显示，并呈现 iOS 26 的液态玻璃界面效果。iOS 26 设置界面采用液态玻璃技术，横跨 Surface Duo 2 的两块屏幕。不过，该项目仍处于早期研究阶段：壁纸显示异常、Wi‑Fi 和蓝牙信息为空，部分界面还存在图形错误；电话应用的数字键盘也会被机身铰链遮挡。在运行于 Surface Duo 2 上的 iOS 26 中设置壁纸。iOS 26 手机键盘的中间一列被 Surface Duo 2 的铰链遮挡住了。Surface Duo 2 上的 iOS 通话屏幕。Surface Duo 2 上的 iOS 26 通讯录屏幕仍然存在图形错误。微软已于 2024 年 10 月停止支持 Surface Duo 2，但这一移植项目让这款被放弃的设备重新获得关注。开发者表示，项目耗时约两个月，过程中也借助 AI 工具理解 XNU 内核的部分机制。下一步，他计划让 Surface Pen 模拟 Apple Pencil，并尝试移植 iOS 27。他计划让 Surface Pen 模拟 Apple Pencil，并尝试移植 iOS 27。相关阅读：《铺路铺到苹果家：开发者成功令微软 Surface Duo 2 运行 iOS / iPadOS 26 系统》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，特斯拉的 Robotaxi 无人驾驶出租车已经能够自行驶入超级充电站，但目前仍需要工作人员手动插上充电枪。未来，这项工作可能交由特斯拉的人形机器人 Optimus 完成。在近期接受 Munro Live 采访时，特斯拉车辆工程副总裁拉尔斯 · 莫拉维（Lars Moravy）和 Cybercab 项目负责人埃里克 · 厄利（Eric Earley）表示，特斯拉计划利用 Optimus 人形机器人为 Robotaxi 插拔充电枪，同时继续研发自动化程度更高的无线充电系统。两人表示：“希望 Optimus 很快就能帮我们完成这项工作。”目前仍由人工为无人驾驶出租车充电目前，特斯拉仍在依靠工作人员为无人驾驶 Robotaxi 手动充电。近期，一段拍摄于美国奥斯汀超级充电站的视频显示，特斯拉员工会在 Cybercab 和 Model Y 无人驾驶出租车抵达后，为车辆插上充电枪。如果车辆没有停在足够靠近充电桩的位置，工作人员还会将其挪动到合适的位置。现阶段，超级充电站是 Cybercab 唯一可用的充电选择，因为这款车型不支持交流充电。因此，Cybercab 仍在后保险杠内隐藏了一个采用北美充电标准（NACS）的充电接口。莫拉维和厄利在采访中解释称，之所以保留充电接口，是因为至少在现阶段，Cybercab 仍需要使用已经建成的充电基础设施。无线充电仍是最终目标Optimus 在这项计划中扮演的角色更像是一种过渡方案。特斯拉表示，随着新基础设施逐步建设，公司正在研发自动化程度更高的充电方式，而 Cybercab 在设计之初就已考虑对这类技术的支持。IT之家注意到，今年早些时候，特斯拉已获得美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）对 Cybercab 无线充电方案的批准。该公司还计划在奥斯汀建设一座 Robotaxi 充电枢纽，配备 80 个无线充电装置。一旦这套系统投入使用，车辆就不再需要人工或 Optimus 机器人插拔充电枪。不过，这一目标短期内恐怕难以实现。特斯拉近期才刚刚在弗里蒙特工厂启动 Optimus 人形机器人的早期生产，首批交付企业客户的计划时间为 2027 年。即使 Optimus 在此之前就开始进入 Robotaxi 充电站工作，从目前的进度来看，Cybercab 无线充电技术也很可能无法在明年落地。特斯拉甚至可能还需要更长时间，才能让这套系统达到实际运营所需的成熟度和可靠性。机器人早已是特斯拉计划的一部分特斯拉计划在 Robotaxi 服务中使用机器人，并非近期才有的想法。此前，该公司已经展示过用于清洁汽车的机器人，并开始在 Robotaxi 运营枢纽安装相关设备。这些枢纽将成为无人驾驶出租车车队的集中停靠点，车辆可在行程间隙在此充电，并接受日常维护。不过，这是特斯拉首次明确提及将 Optimus 纳入 Robotaxi 的运营流程。机器人的用途可能不止于充电。当被问及 Optimus 是否还会帮助维护车队时，莫拉维和厄利表示，它“可能会负责车辆维护，也可能会参与配送领域的工作”。两人还将 Cybercab、Optimus 和 Robovan 视为物理人工智能发展的重要代表，并表示：“这三者的组合将会非常出色。”目前，特斯拉员工仍将继续手动为 Robotaxi 充电。随着 Optimus 逐步进入超级充电站工作，特斯拉下一步还需要在各个 Robotaxi 运营市场推广无线充电技术，最终实现从车辆自动驶入充电区域到完成补能的全流程自动化。

articles.title: 曝“飞行相机鼻祖”零零无限估值达 10 亿美元，跻身独角兽行列
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，据雷峰网今日爆料，“飞行相机鼻祖”零零无限最新一轮融资估值已达 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 66.81 亿元人民币），跻身独角兽行列。据接近零零无限的人士估算，公司今年四季度收入预计约达六七个亿。而此前信息披露，2025 年零零营收已突破 10 亿元人民币。报道称，零零无限今年共披露两轮融资，其中包括博裕资本、襄禾资本、德联资本等在内的 D 轮融资，以及蚂蚁集团旗下公司的 D+ 轮融资。而据接近零零无限的投资人透露，目前要和公司谈融资，tittle 必须是机构合伙人级别。IT之家查询公开资料了解到，零零无限由两位斯坦福大学博士王孟秋和张通在 2014 年共同创立。2016 年，该公司推出了安全易用的便携式无人机 —— Hover Camera Passport（小黑侠），可以说是“飞行相机鼻祖”。该无人机采用全封闭式旋翼结构、碳纤维外壳以及自动跟随拍摄等设计和功能，斩获了 Red Dot 最佳设计奖、IF Design、 CES、DIA 等 30 余项国内外奖项。2019 年，零零无限发布了全新 V 型双旋翼无人机 V-Coptr Falcon（猎鹰）。2022 年，零零无限推出了全新飞行相机品牌 —— 哈浮相机。首款产品哈浮飞行相机 X1 整机重 125g，采用可折叠设计，无需遥控 0 门槛操作、3 秒手掌起降、开机即可起飞拍摄等。

articles.title: 弃用 AI 改称 SI：特斯拉车主手册更新 FSD 计算机名称
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，特斯拉的 FSD 计算机将启用新名称。特斯拉官方车主手册已在多个位置将“FSD Computer”替换为“SI Computer”，涉及 Model 3、Model Y 和 Cybertruck 的相关手册。这似乎是特斯拉正式调整车载计算机命名方式的前兆。按照新的命名规则，HW2.0、HW2.5、HW3 和 AI4 可能分别更名为 SI2.0、SI2.5、SI3 和 SI4。车主手册已经发生变化目前，Model Y 车主手册中的 FSD 相关章节已改为：“Model Y 配备的 SI Computer 旨在利用这些输入信息，快速处理神经网络数据，并做出决策，引导你抵达目的地。”空调控制章节也采用了新名称。手册指出，相关功能“不支持配备 SI Computer 2.0 或 2.5 的车辆”。手册还指导车主：“点击‘控制’（Controls）>‘软件’（Software），查看‘SI Computer’，即可确认车辆配备的计算机型号。”此前，这一选项被称为“AI Computer”。尽管这一名称可能尚未出现在车辆中，但手册的更新暗示，特斯拉可能很快就会通过软件更新，在车辆中控屏幕上启用新的名称。特斯拉为何弃用“AI”？IT之家注意到，此次调整与埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）本月早些时候将 SpaceXAI 更名为 SpaceXSI 的举动一致。SpaceXSI 是 SpaceX Super Intelligence（SpaceX 超级智能）的缩写。此后，Tesla AI 也被调整为 Tesla Super Intelligence，即 Tesla SI。这一变化发生在美国总统唐纳德 · 特朗普（Donald Trump）签署一项行政命令之后。该命令要求行政部门机构在官方材料中使用“Super Intelligence”和“SI”，取代“Artificial Intelligence”和“AI”。尽管马斯克与特朗普此前的关系一度颇为紧张，但从这一系列命名调整来看，马斯克似乎正在跟随美国政府的做法。这并非特斯拉首次调整硬件名称。此前，特斯拉已将 HW4 更名为 AI4，以更好地体现该硬件针对人工智能任务进行优化的定位。HW3 则保留了原有名称，因为其最初并非围绕 AI 任务进行设计。特斯拉已经确认，HW3 无法支持无监督自动驾驶，并计划为搭载 HW3 的车辆提供硬件升级方案，使其能够兼容无监督 FSD。特斯拉副总裁阿肖克 · 埃卢斯瓦米（Ashok Elluswamy）近期表示，特斯拉可能会在 2027 年第二季度开始推出无监督 FSD，并允许车主加入 Robotaxi 无人驾驶出租车网络。下一代 AI5 芯片也可能更名为 SI5新的命名方式还可能应用于未来的硬件产品。特斯拉下一代 AI5 芯片目前已在三星位于美国得克萨斯州的工厂进入试产阶段。按照新的命名规则，该芯片未来上市时可能改称 SI5，后续芯片则可能依次命名为 SI6 等。截至目前，特斯拉尚未正式宣布这项更名计划。不过，如果车主手册的变化能够说明问题，那么在即将推出的软件更新中，车辆中控屏幕上就可能开始出现 SI Computer 这一新名称。

articles.title: “比苹果 Spotlight 更好用”：外媒初探微软 Win11 无 Bing 搜索体验
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（10 月 28 日）发布博文，报道称微软正在向更多 Windows 11 用户，推送“无必应搜索”体验。用户可打开设置应用，在“设置 > 隐私和安全 > 搜索”路径下，关闭网页搜索建议及 Microsoft Store 建议，让开始菜单搜索回归以本地应用、文件、文件夹和系统设置为核心的界面。用户关闭该功能后，搜索首页将不再展示 Bing 热词、小测验、每日冷知识以及 MSN 相关内容，取而代之的是更简洁的最近本地搜索记录。用户也可手动删除不需要的历史条目，减少干扰性推荐。IT之家附上相关截图如下：实际体验方面，关闭网页搜索后，输入关键词可更快匹配本机应用、文件和设置；系统还增强拼写错误的容错能力，例如输入“Otl”或“Putlook”仍可能找到 Outlook。若本机没有匹配内容，用户更可能看到“未找到结果”，而不是跳转网页搜索。该媒体编辑表示他平时还在使用苹果 MacBook，他个人认为在应用检索速度和界面整洁度上，去除 Bing 后的 Windows 搜索体验要优于 macOS Spotlight，不过该结论仍属个人体验。相关阅读：《微软 Win11 预览版优化原生测速体验，不再开浏览器跳转 Bing》《初探 Win11 新版搜索体验：离线也能即时响应，自然语言可直接更改系统设置》《微软展示全新 Win11 搜索体验：从查找文件转向理解用户意图》

articles.title: 柳叶刀倒计时报告：气候变化对人类健康的危害正加速攀升
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，一份于周三发布的全球重要评估报告显示，气候变化对人类健康造成的负面影响不仅日益加剧，而且其恶化速度也比十年前更快。据IT之家了解，这份报告是国际科学家合作项目《柳叶刀倒计时》（Lancet Countdown）发布的第十份年度报告。该项目持续追踪全球变暖与人类健康之间的关系。本次报告对比了《巴黎气候协定》签署前后的两个十年，发现多项重大健康威胁在协定签署后加速恶化，其中包括致命高温和干旱。与此同时，各国也在加大清洁能源投资，并采取措施保护民众免受气候灾害影响。这份报告发布之际，欧洲刚刚经历了一个高温肆虐的夏季，热浪造成数万人死亡。此外，联合国将于近期在土耳其举行第 31 届气候变化大会（COP31）。报告分析发现，2016 年至 2023 年期间，全球每年与高温相关的死亡人数比 2006 年至 2015 年期间高出近 36%。仅在 2023 年一年，高温就与全球约 71 万人死亡有关。高温暴露还在拖累全球各国的国内生产总值，其中东南亚和非洲受到的影响最为严重。《柳叶刀倒计时》首次计算了人为气候变化导致的高温相关死亡人数。研究人员估计，2023 年高温相关死亡病例中，超过 70% 可归因于全球变暖；2016 年至 2023 年期间，这一数字累计接近 300 万人。除了高温，水资源相关风险也在不断上升。2025 年，全球近 52% 的陆地至少经历了一个月的极端干旱，这是有记录以来的第二高水平。一项卫星分析发现，自 2003 年以来，全球约 80% 的陆地区域出现了长期变湿或变干的趋势。这些变化可能威胁农作物生产、饮用水供应和卫生设施的正常运行。当前的厄尔尼诺现象预计还将加剧部分地区的干旱状况，其影响可能持续到明年。联合国气候变化框架公约执行秘书西蒙 · 斯蒂尔（Simon Stiell）在一份声明中表示：“气候危机正在对人类健康造成极其严重的破坏性影响。”他指出，相关影响涉及多个方面，从“致命热浪和洪水，到粮食安全问题、污染以及更多疾病”。这份报告由来自数十家机构的 146 名研究人员共同编写。研究人员追踪了 54 项指标，评估气候变化对健康的影响，以及各方为应对这些影响所采取的行动。报告作者呼吁各国政府将健康因素置于气候政策和能源政策的核心位置。报告同时指出，应对气候变化的措施正在带来健康收益。在至少 77 个自 2016 年以来化石燃料相关空气污染有所下降的国家，空气质量改善每年可避免约 32.3 万人死亡。然而，化石燃料目前仍占全球能源供应的 80% 以上，与化石燃料相关的空气污染每年估计导致 270 万人死亡。各国医疗卫生系统应对气候变化的准备工作也有所改善。世界卫生组织（WHO）的 194 个成员国中，目前已有 56 个国家制定了针对气候变化的卫生服务适应计划，而 2015 年这一数字仅为 14 个。致力于减少医疗卫生行业环境影响的组织 Health Care Without Harm 首席执行官艾米丽 · 班克罗夫特（Emily Bancroft）表示，对许多国家而言，如何筹集资金落实这些计划，仍是一项重大挑战。她说：“围绕这项工作的讨论和交流越来越多，这确实令人鼓舞。但要真正实现目标，资金投入方面仍存在明显缺口。”

articles.title: 通用汽车做自动驾驶不放弃雷达，高管称坚持纯视觉是无视物理规律
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，通用汽车计划最迟在 2028 年推出高速公路自动驾驶功能，但并不打算效仿特斯拉放弃雷达等传感器、转而采用纯视觉方案的做法。当地时间 27 日，通用汽车首席产品官斯特林 · 安德森接受 The Verge 采访时直言：“如果只依靠摄像头，根据物理规律，某些情况下就会出问题。雷达本来就很便宜，根本没必要取消。非要取消雷达，简直是无视物理规律的奇怪信仰执念。”通用汽车计划在 2028 款凯迪拉克 ESCALADE IQ 上推出升级版 Super Cruise 超级辅助驾驶系统，同时使用雷达、激光雷达和摄像头。特斯拉始终坚持纯视觉自动驾驶技术路线。尽管研发进度远比预想缓慢，马斯克还多次严厉批评采用激光雷达的竞争对手。其他大多数自动驾驶公司则认为，增加传感器是保障安全的关键。Waymo 最近也在博客中明确指出，单靠摄像头远远不够。安德森曾负责特斯拉 Autopilot 自动辅助驾驶项目，随后参与创办自动驾驶公司 Aurora。他认为，摄像头以外的传感器不仅能提升自动驾驶性能，更是必不可少。“激光雷达的工作波长与可见光接近，可以与摄像头系统联合训练，加快性能提升。遇到浓雾，摄像头就看不清了，也没法像雷达那样测量瞬时速度。采用多种传感器显然更加安全，物理规律决定了必须这样做。”通用汽车希望开发的高速公路自动驾驶系统，即使驾驶员睡着也能继续运行，而且不会突然要求驾驶员接管。集团计划先在高速公路上应用，之后再逐步扩展至其他道路。这意味着，新系统需要具备远超普通驾驶辅助系统的能力，增加传感器也就显得更加重要。“我们不会突然要求驾驶员接管。不是‘你先开，现在换我，哎呀，无法识别’这种反复交接的模式。这不是 L3 级自动驾驶。”IT之家从报道中获悉，新系统会提前发出接管提醒，留给驾驶员充足的准备时间，例如提前约 10 分钟开始倒计时。如果驾驶员仍未接管，车辆会驶离高速公路，在出口外安全停车，直到驾驶员接手。

articles.title: OpenAI 开放 ChatGPT 新插件：苹果用户授权后可充当 AI 管家，管理 iCloud 邮件、日程等
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，OpenAI 昨日（10 月 27 日）发布博文，宣布面向所有 ChatGPT 套餐用户，开放 iCloud Mail 与 iCloud Calendar 两项插件。IT之家附上相关视频如下：在适用群体方面，OpenAI 官方宣布适用于所有 ChatGPT 计划用户，涵盖 Free（免费版）、Go、Plus、Pro 等消费者套餐。在适用平台上，包括网页版、桌面版以及 iOS 版 ChatGPT 应用。功能方面，OpenAI 表示经用户授权后，ChatGPT 可读取、检查 iCloud 收件箱，创建和管理邮件，并依据邮件中的会议、航班、日程等信息，直接在 Apple 日历中创建或更新事件。对 iPhone、iPad 和 Mac 用户而言，ChatGPT 能更深入地参与日常事务：例如从邮件中识别会议时间并自动建日程、整理行程、起草回复或提醒待办事项。OpenAI 表示，此举显著提升了 ChatGPT 与 iCloud 邮件及 Apple 日历的兼容性。科技媒体 AppleInsider 指出，这一更新也引发隐私与竞争层面的讨论。用户需要明确授权 ChatGPT 访问邮件和日历；而邮件中往往包含账户、行程、财务与工作敏感信息，权限边界和数据处理方式将成为普通用户最关心的问题。

articles.title: 国产脑机接口公司脑虎科技完成 7 亿元 B 轮融资，国投聚力、深创投、勤智资本领投
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，今天（28 日）上午，国产脑机接口公司 NeuroXess 脑虎科技宣布完成 7 亿元人民币 B 轮融资。本轮融资由国投聚力、深创投、勤智资本联合领投，中芯聚源、黄浦投资、基石资本、IDG 资本、曦晨资本、钧犀资本、华福证券、华赛智汇、众为资本、江西金控等知名机构跟投，盛大、中平资本等机构持续支持。据悉，本轮融资资金将用于“三全（IT之家注：全植入、全无线、全功能）”脑机接口系统的多中心临床试验及注册审批、超级工厂量产建设，以及下一代产品研发与 BCI+AI 融合探索。本轮融资将重点用于四大方向：“三全”系统多中心注册临床试验及注册审批、超级工厂量产建设、下一代产品研发，以及 BCI 与 AI 融合方向的持续探索。下一代产品研发将聚焦语言脑机接口的持续迭代与性能优化，并加速视觉脑机接口研发进程，进一步拓展技术适应症边界；BCI+AI 融合方向则将围绕意图调用 AI、连接工具、驱动环境等方向持续投入，探索 BCI+AI 真实物理世界模型，在真实场景中持续获取大脑活动数据，拓展下一代人机交互入口的更多可能。脑虎科技目标在两年内推动产品实现医疗市场规模化落地，让前沿技术真正惠及更多患者。脑虎科技介绍说，本轮融资的另一显著特征，是跨赛道头部资本的集中入场。深耕半导体产业链的头部产业资本中芯聚源，长期聚焦硬科技全周期的知名私募股权投资机构基石资本，以及顶级综合风投 IDG 资本的入局，共同构成了多元化的顶级投资矩阵。同时，盛大、中平资本等老股东的持续支持，进一步印证了资本市场对脑虎科技的长期信心。

articles.title: 苹果 MacBook Neo 2 笔记本曝光：2027 年上半年见，内存升级至 12GB
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，彭博社昨日（10 月 27 日）报道称苹果正在筹备第二代 MacBook Neo，预计将在 2027 年上半年发布。初代 MacBook Neo 于 2026 年 3 月上市，凭借较低价格和便携定位迅速成为苹果的热门产品。报道指出，其市场表现超出预期，也促使外界普遍认为苹果会尽快推出后续机型。从已知传闻看，MacBook Neo 2 的核心升级可能集中在性能与内存：新机或将搭载 A19 处理器，并将基础内存从现款的 8GB 提升至 12GB。现款 MacBook Neo 采用 A18 Pro 芯片和 8GB 内存；若传闻属实，新款在多任务、网页浏览、轻度创作及 AI 相关应用中的体验有望更从容。外观方面，报道称新机可能带来全新配色。目前 MacBook Neo 提供腮红粉、柑橘黄、靛蓝和银色四种选择，新一代机型的色彩策略或将继续面向学生、轻办公用户和首次购买 Mac 的消费者。价格方面仍存在不确定性。初代 MacBook Neo 最初提供 599 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4,002 元人民币）和 699 美元（现汇率约合 4,670 元人民币）两档，但 2026 年 6 月苹果以全球芯片短缺为由，将两档售价均上调 100 美元（现汇率约合 668.1 元人民币）。若供应链压力缓解，MacBook Neo 2 有望维持现价。

articles.title: 苹果 M6 iMac 细节：2.5Gb 网口藏进电源适配器，标准版选配需加价 200 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，苹果昨日（10 月 27 日）推出搭载 M6 芯片的新款 24 英寸 iMac，起售价为 12,499 元。其中一个值得关注的变化，就是将 2.5Gb 以太网端口作为可选配置提供。与以往将网口集成在机身不同，新款 iMac 的以太网端口被整合进配套电源适配器中，用户在购买时选择该选项后，即可通过电源线同时完成供电与有线网络连接。IT之家查询苹果中国官网，在标准款 M6 iMac（2 个雷雳端口、10 核中央处理器、10 核图形处理器、双 16 核神经网络引擎）上，默认没有配备 2.5Gb 以太网端口选项，用户可以额外支付 200 元选配。不过更高配置的 12 核 CPU、12 核 GPU 机型则已标配 2.5Gb 以太网，无需额外付费，该产品起售价为 13,999 元。科技媒体 MacRumors 指出，对于普通用户而言，是否值得加价取决于使用环境。若家中或办公室已部署千兆以上网络、需要稳定低延迟连接，或经常进行大容量数据传输，内置 2.5Gb 网口会更为方便。相关阅读：《苹果为 24 英寸 iMac 推出 M6 芯片版本，国行 12499 元起》

articles.title: Dense Representation Learning and Differentiable Shape Modeling for Spine Landmark Detection
articles.content: Spine landmark detection from spinal X-ray is a key step for estimating spine deformation severity, for building biomechanical models, and for pre-operative planning. We reframe anatomical landmark detection as a pixel-level contrastive representation learning problem, matching dense pixel embeddings with landmark prototypes. Surprisingly, even with a generic U-Net backbone, this formulation results in more discriminative heatmaps compared to the traditional heatmap regression paradigm, leading to improved discrimination between vertebral corners on distinct vertebra. Furthermore, we combine the resulting heatmaps with learnable shape priors over the global configuration of spinal landmarks to resolve ambiguities in landmark locations, yielding a simple and practical approach to spinal landmark detection. Our approach is competitive, in terms of landmark accuracy and clinical parameter estimation, with the state-of-the-art on the public AASCE dataset and on two private spinal X-ray datasets. Our code and pre-trained weights are available at https://github.com/BioMedTP/Pix2Point.

articles.title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models
articles.content: Hybrid language models keep a key-value (KV) cache only in their few full-attention layers, but this cache is still the part of a prompt's state that grows with the prompt and that must be stored or moved to reuse it. We present DCKV, a differentiable codec for the KV cache and the first KV-cache codec that is trained end to end. Its transform, its quantizer and its entropy models, which are conditioned on the prompt tokens and on already decoded neighbouring positions, are optimized together against the frozen language model, both for the code length that the entropy models assign and for the change of the model's output. On Qwen3.5-2B, DCKV stores a compressed token in more than 55 times fewer bytes than bf16 at a loss of at most 1.8 points on three long-context benchmarks, and in more than 100 times fewer bytes at a loss of at most 3.6 points.

articles.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models
articles.content: A large language model maintains conversational content in an external storage that is outside the model and grows as the dialogue continues. This work assumes an environment where a language model has no external memory and no prior knowledge of the future question or its answer. The motivation is to research whether a dialogue can be stored in the model parameters and later answer a question about it. This work proposes self-keyed in-parameter memorization (SKIM), a closed-form method in which the model generates its own questions about each dialogue turn and writes those questions into its parameters as the keys that later retrieve the turn's content. Generating many varied questions for each turn allows a later user question to match one even when phrased differently, and its answer is recalled from the parameters alone. Evaluated on five language models, SKIM recalls most stored dialogue turns from later user questions, and it answers from the model parameters without any external storage.

articles.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance
articles.content: Can additional specialist language-model contexts improve software assurance when deterministic tool evidence is already available? We study this question through five experiments spanning authored Java warning controls, OWASP Benchmark assessment, Defects4J test generation, SV-COMP assertion verdicts, and deliberately misleading evidence packages. The evaluated systems use Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, with a 1.5B sensitivity analysis, and complete 13,638 model requests. On eight related development warnings, increasing the context count from 1 to 50 increases token use 49-fold without improving unsafe clearance. On 160 OWASP cases, model configurations trade clearance against unresolved outcomes; the ten-context arm assesses only 96 cases. On 32 SV-COMP tasks, raw verifier feedback raises mean correct model verdicts from 12.7 to 22.0, but also raises incorrect verdicts from one to seven; a JBMC-plus-JVM validation baseline returns 26 correct verdicts and six unresolved outcomes. On two sets of 120 evidence packages, models reject 70-100% of applicable counterexamples, while construction-specific scope checks classify every package correctly. No target defect is discovered in three Defects4J bugs, one unsupported by the test adapter. These descriptive results support deterministic evidence admission for the tested settings, while exposing limits of verdict aggregation, feedback interpretation, and the available evaluation coverage.

articles.title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation
articles.content: Machine learning recommendations are often evaluated one model at a time, despite deployment across interconnected decision makers. For continuous NPK fertilizer prescriptions, correlated errors can aggregate across farms and generate systemic costs. A model of shared and farm-specific recommendation errors links expected social loss to model adoption shares; the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index characterizes concentration effects when common model errors are independent and predictive risks are equal. A covariance-generalized formulation captures the dependence between model families. A two-model threshold characterizes when privately optimal monoculture is socially dominated, and a convex portfolio rule limits average private predictive regret. Nine model families across five Moroccan cereal systems provide a benchmark-based calibration. Under illustrative parameters and a 10% regret cap, accuracy-constrained diversification lowers modeled social loss in all five systems by 10.89-41.53% (mean 19.41%). Uniform allocation reduces modeled loss in this setting, but breaches the regret cap in every crop. Correlation sensitivity shows that highly dependent model errors attenuate the benefits of diversification. These counterfactual outcomes are not estimates of agronomic or monetary welfare; the framework identifies adoption architecture and error dependence as ecosystem-level evaluation variables.

articles.title: TDLM: Adaptive Temporal Integration for Diffusion Language Models
articles.content: Masked diffusion language models repeatedly compute representations for unresolved tokens, but conventional denoisers do not explicitly retain these representations for reuse across steps. We introduce Temporal Self-Conditioning Diffusion Language Model (TDLM), which lets each unresolved position attend to its own history of hidden representations within a frozen denoiser. This gives later predictions access to computation already performed. Training uses self-generated trajectories and a simple cross-entropy objective for tokens revealed between consecutively sampled decoding steps, while causal temporal attention permits parallel evaluation during training. On LLaDA, the temporal modules add only approximately 0.84% trainable parameters. Across LLaDA and Dream, the main comparison shows up to 7.15$\times$ faster generation than the corresponding original diffusion language model, with competitive answer quality on the evaluated tasks. These results motivate temporal memory as a practical way to make more effective use of repeated denoising computation.

articles.title: JevRec: Linguistic Encoding with Jev-like Decision Modeling for LLM-based Generative Recommendation
articles.content: Generative recommendation (GR) represents items as semantic identifiers (SIDs) and autoregressively generates the next item's SID from interaction history. However, most methods assign the same SID length to all items despite highly unequal interaction frequencies. This uniform design repeatedly incurs the cost of fine-grained codes for popular items, while shortening codes to reduce this cost also compresses the semantic representations of long-tail items. Inspired by the compact forms of frequent expressions in natural language, we propose JevRec to encode items as variable-length words and generate the next item from interaction context. Linguistic encoding retains frequency-dependent semantic prefixes from shared codebooks, producing shorter SIDs for popular items and richer descriptions for long-tail items. Yet predicting a sequence-level length and generating token-level content impose different optimization requirements that may conflict under a shared output head. Our Jev-like decision modeling component therefore predicts a length distribution with a dedicated head and generates content conditioned on length through a separate head while sharing the interaction-history representation. Experiments on three public datasets show that JevRec outperforms all compared baselines across the evaluated recommendation metrics. Further analyses show lower training and inference time than TIGER and reduced gradient conflict between length and content prediction.

articles.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization
articles.content: Optimizing discrete allocation weights across competing segments of a shared budget is a fundamental challenge in resource-constrained, sequential decision-making environments. In practice, this optimization is often hindered by delayed, noisy, and aggregate feedback, alongside strict operational constraints on how frequently weights can be adjusted. Because of the resulting combinatorial action space and extreme data sparsity, classical multi-armed bandit algorithms that evaluate arms independently are rendered highly inefficient. To overcome these limitations, we propose a segmentation-agnostic approach utilizing Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (GP-UCB) algorithms. By placing a Gaussian Process prior on the reward function, our method effectively shares information across neighboring configurations, drastically reducing the necessary exploration horizon. In this paper, we bridge the gap between theoretical bandit research and production-scale deployment. We first introduce a high-fidelity synthetic simulator to evaluate various kernel configurations under stationary, drifting, and reactive environments, identifying a composite Matérn + Linear kernel as the most robust choice for overcoming local noise and global shifts. Finally, we validate our findings through a large-scale Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) in a live production environment. Our empirical results demonstrate that the GP-UCB approach delivers a statistically significant efficiency lift compared to a standard $\varepsilon$-greedy baseline, offering a highly practical solution for real-world black-box lever optimization.

articles.title: Provenance Signatures for Low Rank Adaptations of Image Diffusion Models
articles.content: Diffusion models have revolutionized the generation of realistic artificial images. Efficient techniques such as Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can modify these models for particular use cases, making them more diverse and widely usable. At the same time, open base models may be adapted to deliver biased, harmful or illegal images in an online service. In this paper, we develop a protocol to detect when a service may be using an adaptation of an otherwise standard model. We describe the precise setup and threat model for this provenance question and define two different problems arising due the presence of multiple model families and multiple adaptations. In contrast to previous works that have considered model identification within lists of known candidate models, we consider the realistic open world scenario where the set of possible adaptations and alternative models are unknown. Using a hypothesis testing approach, our protocols can distinguish between the base model, a LoRA adaptation and other completely different families of models. For this test, we develop a black box signature of the models based only on intrinsic dimension of sets of images generated by the models.

articles.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding
articles.content: Multimodal transformer models have driven unprecedented performance breakthroughs in modern document understanding. However, the inherent black-box nature of these models remains a major obstacle to their safe deployment in high-stakes sectors. Despite significant progress in explainability for vision and language tasks, explainable AI (XAI) research tailored to multimodal document understanding has received little attention. To address this gap, we present \ourframework{}, the first comprehensive explainability framework that adapts existing XAI methods and evaluation metrics to the multimodal (text, layout, and image) document understanding context, while introducing efficient multi-target adaptations of both methods and metrics for domain-specific tasks such as semantic entity recognition. Using \ourframework{}, we systematically evaluate 13 XAI methods across 3 document understanding tasks, 8 datasets, 4 models, and 17 evaluation metrics, and find that only a few methods perform consistently across all evaluation criteria, with Occlusion emerging as the most faithful and interpretable method overall. Through a dedicated meta-evaluation, we observe moderate to strong agreement among several faithfulness and complexity metrics while identifying certain ones that produce unreliable results. Finally, through multiple dataset-wide diagnostic analyses, we uncover key insights into model behavior, including the contribution of individual modalities across tasks and labels, spatial attribution patterns around target entities, and potential dataset biases. Overall, this work serves as both a benchmark and a practical guide for future XAI research in multimodal document understanding. To support reproducibility, we publicly release our code at https://github.com/saifullah3396/docxeval/.

articles.title: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds
articles.content: Learning from experience is essential for building the next generation of agents that continually expand their capabilities. Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) already internalize rich world knowledge, yet this knowledge is rarely leveraged to drive policy improvement through online interaction. Realizing this potential efficiently remains challenging, as policy updates shift the agent's interaction distribution, requiring the world model to adapt accordingly, while continually updating large pretrained models is computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we introduce Dwell, a model-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework that reframes a VLM as a recurrent latent transition operator, endowing it with the ability to predict, adjust, and act in latent space. Leveraging the VLM's own representations and its dual role as both world model and policy, the agent continually learns from real interactions to anticipate and evaluate action outcomes, and from latent imagination to improve its behavior. Across five interactive visual environments, Dwell achieves the strongest overall performance among trainable methods while substantially reducing the compute required for imagination, showing that effective world models for VLM agents need not reconstruct the future; they need to predict futures that are useful for action. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tom111-lhx/Dwell

articles.title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces
articles.content: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on memory systems to leverage long-term interactions, yet existing systems typically retrieve memories based on their relevance to the current query and use them as contextual evidence. However, relevance alone does not characterize how a memory contributes to task solving: the same memory may serve different roles across tasks, such as directly supporting the answer or linking to complementary memories with weaker semantic relevance but necessary information. We therefore reframe agent memory systems as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces, where memories are selected and organized by their task-oriented roles and relations. Based on this view, we propose TrawMem, which organizes interaction histories into local threads and constructs task-oriented workspaces by assigning roles and jointly selecting complementary memories. Experiments on LoCoMo and MemGallery with four open- and closed-source backbones show consistent improvements over representative memory systems, with macro-F1 gains of 2.23-3.14 points. On LoCoMo, TrawMem improves the LLM-Judge score over SimpleMem by 4.07 and 4.31 percentage points on Qwen3.5-9B and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, respectively, while requiring approximately 12.8% and 5.1% fewer context tokens, respectively.

articles.title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG
articles.content: When the sources retrieved for a query disagree, the right response depends on why they disagree: a question with several valid answers, a contested topic, stale information and a false source each call for different behaviour. Cattan et al. (2025) showed that telling a generator the conflict type improves its responses by about 24 points, but that predicting the type is hard even for frontier LLMs. We study whether typed decision models, which return probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass instead of generating text, can do this classification fast and cheaply. Using the CONFLICTS benchmark and the original paper's prompt verbatim, we evaluate all 11 decision models served by one commercial inference gateway, from 7 providers, against Gemini models on identical inputs. Asked directly, the decision models reach 50.0--67.0% accuracy; 10 of the 11 match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash, the paper's model (61.3%), at 4--39x lower billed cost (2 were free) and 2.6--6.0x lower latency. The current Gemini 3.8 Flash (70.0%) is significantly more accurate than 8 of them, but sending each decision model's least confident quarter of queries to it gives a cascade statistically tied with it for 8 of the 11, at 25--37% of its cost. End to end, answers generated with the types of 10 of the 11 follow the expected behaviour as often as with the LLM's types. Decomposing the taxonomy into yes/no questions lowers accuracy for every model, and a repair fitted on one model does not transfer. Pre-specified diagnostics show that dates play no measurable role and that sensitivity to source order varies widely between models. Decision models detect a planted false source less reliably than the LLM as hard labels, but their probabilities still separate planted from clean sources. We release code, prompts and all model outputs at https://github.com/Parv17k/decision-models-conflict-typing.

articles.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque
articles.content: Although the recent development of LLMs has paved the way for multi-modal interaction, minority languages face difficulties keeping pace. This work presents the first open Speech Language Model for Basque, designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction. Based on the LLaMA-Omni architecture, the system integrates a Latxa model as its backbone, transferring its Basque capabilities to the spoken modality by fine-tuning several modules. To address data scarcity, the English VoiceAssistant-400K corpus was translated into Basque, and the audio was synthesized using a Basque TTS. Evaluation results confirm the system's viability, achieving 3.86/5 in content quality, a 9.94% WER for spoken intelligibility, and a 3.07 UTMOS for audio quality. This work demonstrates that advanced spoken interaction systems can be developed using modular architectures and synthetic data even in low-resource languages.

articles.title: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence from a Large Randomized Evaluation Corpus
articles.content: Many AI systems need to find every relevant items in a large collection and then organize what they found. The standard way to do this is to tag each item with labels from a curated vocabulary and search on those labels. Those labels are useful for organizing results, but searching on them misses items that do not fit a label and returns too much when labels are broad. We compare this approach with an embedding-based approach: find candidates by meaning using text embeddings, then have a language model keep only the relevant ones. In a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, label search found 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the new approach found 92%, at a cost per query that rises with search depth. These results support a two-stage architecture that combines broad candidate retrieval with query-specific evidence filtering.

articles.title: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
articles.content: We propose HiLo-RD (High-to-Low Budget Representation Distillation) to improve masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) under a limited generation budget. Unlike autoregressive models, MDLMs choose both what to generate and where to commit it. This creates two coupled challenges: predicting useful content before reasoning is complete, and deciding when to fix answer tokens that shape later predictions. We identify budget-induced premature commitment: even when a correct solution fits, the model can fix answer fragments near the window boundary before resolving intermediate steps. These fragments become context for later predictions and redirect subsequent reasoning. Existing post-training methods do not directly transfer the stronger trajectories that the same model follows with a larger window. HiLo-RD addresses this gap by (1) pairing large-window teacher states with cropped small-window views and (2) matching their hidden representations at committed positions. This supervision guides both token prediction and commitment order without an external teacher. Across mathematics benchmarks, HiLo-RD improves low-budget accuracy and shortens responses; these gains extend to code generation without code-domain training. On GSM8K, accuracy rises by 9.4 percentage points as mean readable length falls by about 25%. Attention diagnostics and fixed-budget order interventions support the proposed mechanism. Together, these results show that large-window reasoning can improve small-window decoding.

articles.title: Natural Hard-Negative Mining from Positives for Instruction-Following Retrieval
articles.content: Instruction-following information retrieval (IFIR) requires retrievers to rank documents by both a query and its instance-specific instructions, yet instruction-conditioned contrastive supervision remains scarce. Existing synthetic methods typically fix a positive passage and generate additional negatives, overlooking the hard-negative potential of the original positive. We propose Natural Hard-Negative Mining (NHNM), which promotes convertible negatives under query-compatible instructions and repurposes original positives as natural instruction hard negatives. Its automated Candidate Cleaning, Reversal Construction, and Geometry Filtering pipeline produces compact, high-contrast supervision aligned with the pretrained retrieval space. Applied to MSMARCO, NHNM yields NHNM-MARCO, an IFIR training set of nearly 7K instances. On InstructIR and FollowIR, models with 568M to 4B parameters fine-tuned on NHNM-MARCO achieve strong instruction-following performance and match or surpass substantially larger retrievers in several settings. Controlled analyses and ablations attribute these gains to natural hard-negative supervision rather than model scale or training-data volume.

articles.title: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets
articles.content: We present PREEN (Preset Regression via an Exemplar-based Editor Network), which casts color style transfer as regression onto the 29 parameters of a deterministic image editor. Given a content image and a style reference, PREEN predicts a preset, a vector of editor slider values that is interpretable and editor-consumable, not a raster image. The key obstacle is supervision, since an arbitrary real reference lacks a preset ground truth. We therefore supervise with a style-transfer teacher, whose target looks we invert into the editor's parameter space as pseudo-presets, then pretrain a CLIP-conditioned regressor and refine it with LoRA under an image-level CIELAB loss. On the human-curated PST50 benchmark, PREEN applies the reference's color while preserving structural fidelity, leading the baselines on pixel- and perceptual-fidelity metrics. The preset is compact and predicted at sub-second on-device latency. The low-dimensional subspace also exposes a single inference-time strength knob that traces a continuous default-to-vivid trajectory in one forward pass, with every intermediate state a valid editor preset. A two-axis human study shows that raters prefer the vivid end for matching the reference but the default as a standalone photo, a trade-off the knob spans without retraining.

articles.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and the noise emission directivity. This leads to over-conservative policies and unexploited wind power. Yet, turbine yaw can simultaneously affect wake interactions and the direction of noise emission, offering an additional degree of freedom for farm-level noise control. We therefore propose Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximise farm power while satisfying a local noise constraint in a defined region. To enable training at a reduced computational cost, a low-fidelity acoustic model is coupled with the steady-state FLORIS simulator. The RL agent effectively learns how to redirect wakes and noise directivity away from the protected region while redistributing power across the farm. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfies the 40 dB noise constraint throughout the full range of turbulent winds, with an average power deficit of only 2% relative to greedy unimpeded control, and up to 7.7% at high wind speeds. In comparison, the industry-standard noise-reduced operation (NRO) baseline here generates an average power loss of 17%. When deployed in the higher-fidelity FAST.Farm simulator, the policy largely retains its performance under steady and turbulent inflow, despite differences in simulation fidelity. These results demonstrate the potential of combining yaw control and power derating through RL to improve the power-noise trade-off in wind farm operation.

articles.title: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL
articles.content: In this study, we propose a dual-branch evolutionary framework that simultaneously performs Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) for Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Autonomous Driving (AD) tasks. While NAS has shown strong potential in automating architecture design for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), its application to RL remains limited, especially in scenarios that require joint optimization of architectural and training dynamics. Building on our prior work on Evolutionary Multi-Objective NAS (EMNAS), the proposed framework evolves discrete network architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective search strategy. In this setup, NAS targets the convolutional layers of the RL policy network - responsible for visual feature extraction, while HPO focuses on optimizing critical RL hyperparameters. To accelerate convergence and improve generalization, we incorporate parallel evaluation and a teacher-student policy transfer mechanism. Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint NAS-HPO framework consistently outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability. These results highlight the benefits of jointly optimizing model structure and training dynamics for scalable and effective RL agent design.

articles.title: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction
articles.content: Channel state information (CSI) prediction forecasts future channel states from historical observations, supporting transceiver design and resource allocation with reduced measurement overhead. However, existing deep learning predictors mainly encode channel knowledge in model parameters, which can limit their ability to represent diverse patterns of channel dynamics across scenes. In this paper, we propose RAG-CSI, a retrieval-enhanced Transformer framework that augments prediction with relevant historical channel knowledge. Specifically, we construct a global--local CSI knowledge store containing representative observations across scenes and historical observations from the current serving scene. We further develop joint state--dynamics retrieval (JSDR), which jointly characterizes channel states, phase dynamics, and amplitude dynamics to retrieve relevant CSI sequences. A Transformer predictor then uses cross-attention to fuse the retrieved knowledge with the current CSI history and predict future CSI with limited additional model parameters. Experiments on a multi-scene CSI dataset show overall improvements exceeding 10\% across all five evaluation metrics over the best baseline for each metric, including a 15.42\% reduction in normalized mean squared error.

articles.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents
articles.content: Deep research agents conduct multi-step Web searches and synthesise retrieved information into analytical reports. Evaluating these outputs requires checking which analyses they deliver, beyond the presence of relevant facts. Query-specific binary rubrics make individual requirements explicit, but task-level checklists may leave the overall analytical structure underexamined. We introduce RubricAtlas, which derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports on different objects within the same research type and organises detailed checks around recurring analytical questions. The requirements give related tasks a shared standard for what to analyse, without prescribing their answers. Our framework links binary checkpoints to report passages and evaluates completeness separately from argument validity. Built from 3,079 Chinese financial research reports, RubricAtlas covers 99 research types. Reference-report selection experiments show that individual reports cover only about half of their type's analytical questions, and that selecting requirements from different reports changes evaluation scores and agent rankings. Across ten agents, two judge pipelines achieve checkpoint agreement of $κ$ = 0.71 and agent-ranking agreement of Kendall $τ$ = 0.87. Controlled deletions reduce scores on the affected analyses, while padding produces no detectable increase. These findings support type-level rubrics for comparing the analytical completeness of Web deep research outputs, with individual decisions traceable to report evidence.

articles.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
articles.content: Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text. However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry. To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots. Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token. We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics. On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8-4.0x faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA

articles.title: HoloRecon: Incremental Reconstruction of Long-Range Panoramas with Global Consistency
articles.content: Long-sequence panoramic reconstruction requires detailed scene geometry and globally consistent camera poses across distant revisits. Panoramic SLAM and incremental SfM rely on feature correspondences, but repeated, similar structures and small partial overlap make reliable long-range connections difficult to establish, leaving accumulated drift unresolved. Feed-forward models offer detailed local geometry, but their high computational costs limit inference window size, necessitating additional constraints for global consistency. This motivates combining continuous feature-based tracking and sparse mapping with rapid, high-quality local reconstruction from feed-forward models to achieve accurate localization and globally consistent dense mapping over long sequences. We therefore propose a panoramic reconstruction framework that couples an ORB-based sparse panoramic mapping frontend with a fine-tuned feed-forward model. Our key insight is that predicted local geometry enables 3D verification of feature matches across distant revisits, yielding long-range camera constraints even between regions. We calibrate predicted depths with sparse landmarks and use verified connections to optimize the global pose graph, updating dense geometry with the corrected camera poses. We also introduce PanoRecon, a seven-scene benchmark with repetitive architecture, large and small loops, and reference camera poses and LiDAR geometry for evaluating global consistency. Our method achieves the lowest mean absolute trajectory error and high F-1 Score among the evaluated methods. Project Page:https://zhuoxiaoli.github.io/HoloRecon_page/

articles.title: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding
articles.content: GUI grounding on high-resolution screens fails mostly on small targets, and zooming in is a common training-free remedy. However, most existing zooming pipelines do not match the zoom to the target's size, accept the zoomed answer unconditionally and never revisit a wrong answer. To address these issues, we propose AdaGround, a training-free framework with three components: (1) Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming, which sets the magnification, field of view and zoom depth of each sample from the model's own estimate of the target size; (2) Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement, which uses one marked-click Yes/No verifier to keep or reject each zoom, choose between zoom chains, trigger re-grounding and, with an existence query, decide when to abstain; and (3) Compositional Structure Grounding, which composes spreadsheet cells from their headers. On Qwen3-VL models, AdaGround surpasses state-of-the-art training-free zooming methods and many trained GUI models, improving accuracy over the backbone by 7.4 to 20.6 points on OSWorld-G and ScreenSpot-Pro, and its gains carry over to held-out UI-Vision. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/AdaGround

articles.title: RangeRectQuant: Compressing Scientific Fields for Every Future Rectangular Sum
articles.content: Scientific rasters are often stored before the regions to be measured are known. Independent pixel-error bounds can force exact integer reconstruction when one absolute error budget covers every future rectangle. Coordinated changes allow every pixel to change while every rectangular sum remains accurate. A prefix sum accumulates values from the top-left corner. Four such sums determine any rectangular total. RangeRectQuant preserves the pixel range and designated exact samples while controlling errors in prefix sums. At each row position, we characterize exactly which errors let the remaining pixels meet these constraints. These errors form a single integer interval, even when many completions exist. A backward pass finds its endpoints; a forward pass uses them to choose quantized pixels. The resulting field meets the prescribed error budget for every axis-aligned rectangle, with linear work and workspace proportional to one row. Experiments on geographically held-out built-surface and water-occurrence maps show substantial storage savings over alternatives meeting the same requirements. Data producers encode once; later users measure arbitrary rectangles without the source, re-encoding, or query-specific correction.

articles.title: Tail Cues, Principal Corrections: Plug-and-Play Rectification for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation
articles.content: Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation (OSTTA) operates on non-stationary target streams where covariate and semantic shifts coexist. Existing TTA methods often obtain adaptation signals by updating model parameters or maintaining mutable memories, which can be costly and vulnerable to unknown samples. We present TALOR, a lightweight, backward-free rectification module that uses the source linear head as a geometric anchor. The head-induced basis decomposes each normalized feature into high-gain principal coordinates and low-gain tail coordinates. TALOR estimates a soft-routed affine correction in the principal subspace, combining a regime-level principal bias with a tail-conditioned slope that captures sample-level tail-to-principal coupling. Using weighted ridge regression, it subtracts this drift estimate from the principal coordinates, reconstructs the feature and feeds it into the source head. On the ImageNet-C benchmark with six csOOD datasets, TALOR outperforms the next-best UniEnt by 2.2% H-score while running 2.5x faster and using only 12% of its GPU memory; as a post-correction plug-in, it further boosts COME to 68.4% H-score with only 2% additional memory overhead.

articles.title: Sample-and-Score: Surrogate-Guided Coordinated Spatial Reuse in IEEE 802.11 Networks
articles.content: Coordinated spatial reuse (Co-SR) in IEEE 802.11bn increases area throughput through simultaneous transmissions, yet the combinatorial configuration space makes real-time optimization challenging. We propose a sample-and-score approach: draw random Co-SR configurations, score each with a surrogate model, and select the best. The surrogate is trained offline and deployed without online fine-tuning or sequential exploration, yet performs close to multi-armed bandit and heuristic baselines that need multiple interaction steps or extensive measurements. On unseen topologies with 2-16 access points, it recovers 52-77% of a perfect surrogate's throughput. A perfect sample-and-score approach reaches 95% of the upper bound throughput with 8192 candidates.

articles.title: Intrinsic Information-Theoretic Analysis of ReLU Nets
articles.content: Mutual information (MI) is fundamental to representation-learning analysis in deep networks, but in high dimensions MI estimators depend on hyperparameters whose bias often dominates the signal. We show that continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) networks, including ReLU networks, admit an intrinsic information-theoretic analysis that avoids this pitfall: their inherent partition of the input space into convex linear regions assigns to every input a discrete region label $Π$ alongside the continuous representation $T$ and label $Y$. We introduce a decomposition of the mutual information $I(Y;T)$ into interpretable geometric terms. We show that the dominant term, the *routing information* $I(Y; Π)$, admits an estimable plug-in estimator, that in the well-sampled regime, approximates a population lower bound on the joint information $I(Y; Π, T)$. When the partition saturates, a functional-equivalence quotient collapses regions implementing the same linear operator and restores informativeness; this extension has a single bounded, dimensionless parameter, which is reported through the quotient's compression ratio. The routing estimator agrees strongly with three established MI baselines applied to the same networks and data. The functional quotient recovers informative estimates in the regime bordering the well-sampled and under-sampled regime. We provide a framework for analysing the internal information geometry of CPWL networks, grounded in their inherent piecewise-linear structure rather than in external discretisation.

articles.title: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks
articles.content: Transition-metal-based batteries rely on critical elements such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Their extraction creates environmental and supply-chain challenges. Organic electrode materials (OEMs) reduce this reliance and provide broad molecular tunability. However, OEM-based batteries still show limited long-term cycling stability. Their design also requires the joint optimization of coupled metrics such as voltage, specific capacity, capacity retention, and energy density. These metrics depend on the full battery stack and on the interactions among its components rather than on the active material alone. In our previous work, we developed a data-fusion multi-task framework for average discharge voltage and first-cycle specific capacity. Both targets are single-valued. Here, we extend that framework to multi-horizon prediction by predicting a property at every cycle of a discharge trajectory rather than at a single cycle. Our multi-fidelity and Multi-horizon Deep Operator Network learns DFT redox potentials and cycle-dependent specific-capacity trajectories within one model. We train it on complete battery-stack representations and usage conditions, so it learns battery-stack interactions rather than cathode-only effects. This framework supports long-term property prediction, inverse design, and process optimization for organic battery systems.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prospect theory splits risky choice into three parts: loss aversion, measured by the relative weight of losses to gains, $\lambda$ (e.g., $\lambda = 2$ implies that losses weigh twice as much as gains), diminishing sensitivity to the size of outcomes (i.e., the curvature and linearity of the value function), and the nonlinear weighting of probabilities. I examined whether Large Language Models (LLMs) display the same properties as people by meta-analyzing 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models. The three components emerge differently. Loss aversion is modest: the pooled $\lambda$ is 1.26 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.46), far below the strongest human meta-analytic estimate ($\lambda = 1.96$) and compatible with more conservative ones (1.07 and 1.31). Abstract: Use-based AI regulation assigns obligations by deployment risk but lacks an evidentiary object to carry them. Abstract: Constraint-based causal discovery relies on conditional-independence (CI) tests that may conflict in finite samples, leaving no causal graph that satisfies them all. articles.content:

Abstract: Alignment evaluations aim to assess whether large language models would engage in dangerous misaligned behaviour. Misaligned and evaluation-aware models might engage in alignment faking, where they pursue a hidden goal, but conceal this behaviour when they suspect effective oversight such as during training, evaluation or audited deployment. Such a model might view any prompt-based intervention that aims to reveal latent propensities as part of the evaluation, calling into question the reliability of existing alignment evaluations. Current methods for detecting alignment faking rely on chain-of-thought monitorability, highly realistic environments that reduce evaluation awareness, or mechanistic interventions, all of which are expected to become less reliable for future model generations. Abstract: Current sign language recognition and translation benchmarks are commonly collected in controlled settings using fixed or studio-style cameras, particularly limiting their ability to reflect how signers communicate in everyday mobile scenarios. Abstract: Current uses of large language models (LLMs) for qualitative coding often rely on ad hoc prompting with limited guidance for reliability and human oversight. articles.content:

Abstract: Frontier AI models are increasingly deployed on topics where the stakes are high and expert judgment is required, including healthcare, defense, finance, governance, and politics. We present a general methodology for distilling expert human judgment into automated evaluation systems that operate at scale. Our approach assembles networks of domain experts and develops techniques for extracting not just their conclusions but their reasoning processes, encoding those processes into structured editorial standards that automated judges can apply continuously. We ground our approach in a long tradition of research on the nature of expertise and the conditions under which expert judgment is reliable and more effective than other approaches, and argue that independent, expert-calibrated evaluation is necessary not only on epistemic grounds but as a matter of accountability and public trust. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33240v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As frontier AI systems increasingly serve as sources of political and current-events information, evaluating the epistemic quality of their responses is now especially consequential. Existing evaluations often focus narrowly on ideological alignment, rely on measures not validated for this setting, or depend on reference labels derived from public opinion or non-expert annotation, potentially producing misleading or miscalibrated results. To address these limitations, we introduce NewsBench, an expert-grounded benchmark that reframes evaluation around editorial standards developed by senior practitioners in journalism, policy, and intelligence analysis. articles.content:

Abstract: Data science agents can automate end-to-end machine learning workflows, yet they remain far from competitive on human leaderboards. Agents make process errors such as insufficient exploration, unsound validation, coding bugs, and poor use of a fixed budget (re-running the same exploratory data analysis and baseline models in every attempt). articles.content:

Abstract: LLMs often answer semantically equivalent queries inconsistently, even when the underlying facts are known. articles.title: TempShap: When and How Much a Feature Matters in Time-Series Forecasting
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attribution for a time-series forecaster should answer two questions that a feature-level scalar cannot: when in the input window a feature acts, and how much its influence changes across the forecast horizon. Most existing Shapley explainers treat each feature as one player and therefore collapse both axes. We propose TempShap, a retrospective, loss-based Shapley framework whose players are the individual input cells $(t,i)$. Its attribution tensor yields temporal-localization and horizon-impact profiles. We validate these against planted temporal structures, a tractable exact cell game, and a closed-form attribution oracle for a real linear forecaster. Abstract: Molecular cloning is one of the most routine wet-lab workflows, yet existing evaluations of language models in biology mostly test knowledge recall or isolated steps rather than end-to-end experimental planning. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise workflow agents typically rely on step-by-step interaction (Step-by-Step): the agent executes an action, observes its result, and invokes a large language model (LLM) again to decide the next step. Global orchestration (Global) instead generates a complete executable workflow in advance and executes it without further LLM calls, substantially reducing inference overhead, but it remains less accurate than Step-by-Step. We study how close Global can come to Step-by-Step and what narrows the remaining gap. We introduce AgentOrch, a benchmark that directly compares global orchestration with step-by-step interaction on 650 enterprise SOPs and 3,220 runtime variants under matched tools, environments, and evaluation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31702v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We propose Poly-Ripple, a framework in which multiple clients perform ICL using large autoregressive vision models (LAVMs) without model updates. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31704v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0. Our analysis highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection as primary physical techniques, while revealing a significant shift toward deep learning and generative models for automated defect recognition. Abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Abstract: Optimizing high-dimensional physical systems under expensive evaluations and complex constraints is a central challenge in science and engineering. In offline model-based optimization (MBO), methods must improve designs using only a fixed dataset and no test-time access to the true objective. Abstract: Microservice systems have become a dominant architecture for large-scale cloud applications, enabling rapid deployment and elastic scaling. However, ensuring the reliability and availability of microservice systems critically relies on effective anomaly detection, as failures and performance anomalies can quickly propagate across services and severely impact end-to-end system behavior. Existing multimodal anomaly detection approaches for microservice systems often struggle with two fundamental limitations: (i) the neglect of modality-specific characteristics in favor of cross-modality fusion, and (ii) the "identity-shortcut" problem that affects the feature reconstruction process. Abstract: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people. articles.content:

Abstract: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates us to investigate structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. We establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extend the analysis to multiple tasks, revealing how task coverage and gradient reliability jointly shape learning. Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict human sentiments by integrating signals from different modalities such as text, video, and audio. However, raw multimodal sequences often suffer from semantic inconsistency--exhibiting redundancy or conflicts within and across modalities--which hinders robust understanding and increases computational cost. To this end, we introduce ConsMSA, which explicitly formalizes semantic distribution consistency across both $\textit{intra}$- and $\textit{inter}$-modality, providing a consistency-aware mechanism for robust and efficient multimodal sentiment prediction. Specifically, ConsMSA projects multimodal token features into a shared sentiment space to compute an Intra- and Inter-modality Consistency Score ($I^2CS$). Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. Intervention-based evaluations measure this property by asking whether a monitor can detect the role of an intervention from the CoT when the targeted behavior occurs, typically using minimal-criterion sensitivity ($\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$) proposed by~\citep{guan2025monitoring}. Specifically, we establish $\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$ as an upper bound on this causal detection rate and derive a complementary lower bound, which provides a tighter evaluation framework for CoT monitorability. Abstract: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video, enabling stronger multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities, but often at substantial inference cost. We observe that the benefit of additional modalities varies across queries, indicating that a fixed modality configuration can be inefficient. Motivated by this, we study query-wise modality selection, which keeps the underlying Omni-LLM fixed while adaptively selecting which modalities to provide for each query. We formulate the problem as an accuracy-cost optimization problem and develop a cost-sensitive learning approach for modality selection. We evaluate our approach on WorldSense using Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni under three inference-cost measures: input tokens, latency, and monetary cost. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31778v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. Compaction is generally lossy by design: agents can silently lose task constraints, instructions, or their reasoning behind earlier decisions. Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks. Previous work evaluate smaller open weight models on toy or synthetic trajectories. We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks (PaperBench, ProgramBench, PostTrainBench). Abstract: Federated unlearning (FU) aims to remove a designated target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch. Existing methods largely treat unlearning as a post-hoc, stateless operation, overlooking that client influence is path-dependent: contributions made during training, particularly during critical learning periods (CLPs), can have disproportionate and persistent effects. Moreover, knowledge overlap and intermittent client availability make relying on all retained clients inefficient and impractical. We introduce PDF, a path-dependent client-selection framework based on the insight that retained clients are not equally valuable for unlearning. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31791v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. Abstract: A bug report describes what went wrong, but rarely where the code should change. Existing repository-level localization methods often let language models iteratively decide what code to inspect next, requiring repeated model calls and substantial token usage. We investigate whether these inspection decisions can instead be planned before source retrieval. In this research, we introduce CuraLoc, which first selects candidate files and represents their symbols using compact behavioral and structural descriptions. In a single planning decision, the model jointly selects starting symbols, chooses code relationships to inspect from each, and forms hypotheses about likely edits. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31818v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. In this work, we explore an alternative mechanism for conditional computation that analogously generalizes the attention operator. The sparsity induced by this mechanism naturally nests (i.e., hierarchically composes) with the sparsity induced by the MoE operator. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. Abstract: Speculative decoding is a technique that accelerates the inference speed of autoregressive large language models (LLMs) by sampling from a faster, lower quality draft model. Traditionally, a fundamental characteristic of speculative decoding is that it is lossless with respect to the verifier distribution, guaranteeing speed without sacrificing quality. This differs from recently developed diffusion LLMs (dLLMs), which are notably able to achieve substantial speedups by degrading the quality of their outputs with less diffusion effort. Because diffusion models are able to sample faster than autoregressive models by generating tokens in parallel, they are considered strong candidates for draft models in speculative diffusion. Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are indispensable tools for modeling complex phenomena in physics and engineering. articles.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback: Mathematical Foundations and Algorithm Design
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31862v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This article provides an introduction to the mathematical foundations and algorithmic frameworks used to align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human intentions, preferences, and values. We discuss standard alignment techniques, such as fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), and direct preference optimization (DPO). We also explore the theoretical underpinnings of learning from human preferences, drawing connections to inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) and discrete choice models. We present state-of-the-art algorithms in a tutorial style, discuss their advantages and limitations, and offer insights into practical implementation. Our exposition is intended to serve as a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners, providing both a foundational understanding of alignment methodologies and a framework for developing more robust and scalable alignment techniques.

Abstract: Academic revision presents a governance problem when legitimate writing objectives conflict. Writing-process and social-science research show that revision is recursive and that wording carries epistemic and disciplinary commitments. Those literatures identify important constraints but do not settle which objective should prevail when concision, outlet form or stylistic variation conflicts with evidence and claim boundaries. This paper models revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints. Task-relative invariants, contextual constraints and mutable presentation choices define the admissible space; a claim-preservation contract links evidence and judgement to an authorised claim boundary. Abstract: Energy-based models have shown promising properties for domain-specific tasks but remain challenging in modeling general-purpose scenarios. To bridge this gap, we design energy-steered models (ESMs) for foundational language modeling. ESMs integrate energy steering and token generation within a single architecture to leverage the energy-guided search to refine token generation. By performing such energy-guided pre-training on large-scale corpora, ESMs learn generally effective energy landscape where favorable tokens correspond to lower energy values. Abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) impose substantial computation and memory costs as context sizes increase, motivating methods that compress a context into a shorter representation before inference. Existing soft-prompt compression methods typically use the same Transformer backbone as used in the target model, where producing the compressed representation leads to significant latency overheads. This restricts them to the offline setting where context is compressed once and then reused across many queries. We propose the Boa Compressor, a plug-and-play online context compressor built on a Mamba state-space model (SSM) that encodes arbitrary-length context in a single linear-time pass, producing a representation on which we condition a frozen target LLM. articles.title: Knowledge-Guided LLM for Intent-Driven Service Orchestration in Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial 6G Networks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33007v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural-language service intents in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial (TN/NTN) 6G networks can be incomplete, ambiguous, or inconsistent, making unconstrained LLM generation challenging for reliable network-facing orchestration. This paper proposes a knowledge-guided LLM framework that combines grammar-constrained semantic parsing with a knowledge-graph (KG)-driven clarification loop to produce validated, orchestration-ready service profiles across four representative service classes. On a 200-sample intent dataset, the framework achieves 89% classification accuracy and 95% policy validity with an average of 0.66 clarification turns per request. Compared with a Pure-LLM baseline, the proposed framework improves policy validity and contradiction detection while requiring fewer clarification turns, demonstrating the value of explicit knowledge-guided reasoning for robust intent processing in integrated TN/NTN 6G orchestration.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33008v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible generation through iterative masked denoising, but incur substantial inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across denoising steps. Existing cache-based methods reduce this cost by reusing intermediate results across denoising steps and recomputing only a subset of positions at each step, chosen either on a fixed schedule or by heuristic signals of change. Our trajectory experiments instead point to decoding trajectory as the more relevant quantity. Cached generation remains accurate when it stays close to the full-denoising trajectory, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations and reduced as longer reference prefixes are recovered. This suggests a more direct principle: limiting representation error helps, but keeping generation on the full-denoising trajectory is a more direct route to accurate decoding. arXiv:2610.33012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use exhibit inconsistent behavior across independent runs from identical states, calling different tools, producing contradictory outputs, or pursuing divergent strategies. This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions. Separately, agent behavior is analyzed either at the token level using probability distributions or at the single-response level using semantic clustering, but neither captures how inconsistency propagates across future turns of a trajectory.
